glosses: To use or spread propaganda.
To tell propaganda to someone in an attempt to influence one's views.

examples.text: After we'd managed to make ourselves comfortable in this garret, my new friends began to propagandize me. All they knew about me was that I was a student […]

glosses: To use something or someone in propaganda purposes.

examples.text: He propagandized this panacea with single-minded determination throughout the revolutionary period and even managed to establish a People's Bank for a short time before his arrest in 1849.

glosses: Someone whose job is to speak for someone's case in a court of law; a counsel.
Anyone who argues the case of another; an intercessor.

examples.text: I neuer did incense his Maiestie / Against the Duke of Clarence, but haue bin / An earnest aduocate to plead for him.

glosses: A person who speaks in support of something, or someone; proponent

examples.text: "I think," replied the young advocate, unwilling to give up a point in which his feelings were interested, "that even you would believe in Walter Maynard's success in life, if you knew him. What has brought the world to its present state, but individual talent?"

glosses: A person who supports others to make their voices heard, or ideally for them to speak up for themselves.

examples.text: Since she started working with her advocate, she has become much more confident.

glosses: To plead in favour of; to defend by argument, before a tribunal or the public; to support, vindicate, or recommend publicly.

glosses: To encourage support for something.

examples.text: I like trees, but I do not advocate living in them.

glosses: To engage in advocacy.

examples.text: We have been advocating for changes in immigration law.
And why has no one in the [rail] industry advocated for a universal requirement for face covering (even if it's just a scarf or old tea towel), [...].

glosses: To appeal from an inferior court to the Court of Session.
To call a case before itself for decision.
To raise (someone) to a more important, responsible, or remunerative job or rank.

examples.text: He promoted his clerk to office manager.

glosses: To advocate or urge on behalf of (something or someone); to attempt to popularize or sell by means of advertising or publicity.

examples.text: They promoted the abolition of daylight saving time.
They promoted the new film with giant billboards.

glosses: To elevate to a higher league.

examples.text: At the end of the season, three teams are promoted to the Premier League.

glosses: To increase the activity of (a catalyst) by changing its surface structure.
